identity.title: Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models

problem.claim: Quantify the capabilities of autonomous cybersecurity language-model agents to support cyber-risk mitigation and investigate penetration-testing opportunities.

contributions.claim: Cybench specifies cybersecurity tasks and evaluates agents on them.
A benchmark of 40 professional-level CTF tasks from four competitions, spanning varied difficulty, with task descriptions, starter files, executable environments, and intermediary subtasks.
An evaluation of eight language models and, for GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, four agent scaffolds.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce Cybench as a framework for specifying and evaluating cybersecurity tasks, including subtasks for more detailed assessment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, without subtask guidance, agents using Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, OpenAI o1-preview, and Claude 3 Opus solved complete tasks that human teams took up to 11 minutes to solve.
The authors report that the most difficult task took human teams 24 hours and 54 minutes to solve.

narrative_sequence.summary: Autonomous agents that identify vulnerabilities and execute exploits may have real-world impact, motivating capability measurement.
Cybench introduces a task-evaluation framework with 40 varied professional-level CTF tasks and executable environments.
Subtasks decompose tasks into intermediary steps because many tasks exceed current agents' capabilities.
The study evaluates eight models and compares four scaffolds for the two top-performing models.
Several models reportedly solved some complete tasks without subtask guidance, alongside a large human-time range across tasks.

source_observation.claim: The framework adds intermediary subtasks when complete tasks are beyond existing agents, enabling more detailed evaluation.

lessons.interpretation: Decomposing an end-to-end challenge can expose partial capability that aggregate task success hides.
lessons.application: For a complex benchmark, report both whole-task outcomes and progress on predefined intermediate steps.
lessons.exception: This is unsuitable when intermediate steps are ambiguous, overly scaffolded, or fail to represent the real end-to-end objective.

unknowns: The abstract gives no per-model scores, task-level results, subtask outcomes, or scaffold comparison results.
It does not specify how success, human solve times, or task difficulty were measured or compared.
